subject: SLA template amendment: phased monthly credits & latency fallback
messages:
From: Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@aurora.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sethi <priya.sethi@aurora.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA template amendment / uptime smoothing request

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we start to scope the pilot with Aurora Analytics' data pipelines, our procurement and platform teams have one ask on the SLA template: we need an initial "smoothing" period for uptime-related credits during ramp. Our concern is the first 60-90 days when traffic patterns are still stabilizing and batch inference windows will produce correlated latency spikes.

Specifically we're proposing:
- a phased monthly credit schedule for the first three months (reduced credit exposure)
- explicit latency fallback carveouts for scheduled batch windows and model warmup (p95/p99 carveouts limited to defined windows)
- a clause for a 30-day operational review after go-live to revisit numbers

I attached a redline of your SLA template with Aurora's comments (Aurora_SLA_Redlines.pdf). Can you share what flexibility Redwood can offer here? We're aiming to keep the commercial terms reasonable while protecting our startup customers during ramp.

Best,
Ethan
Ethan Morales
Head of Platform Engineering
Aurora Analytics

--

Ethan —

Appreciate the redlines and the context. We can be pragmatic here; our goals align: predictable economics for you during ramp, and preserving our availability commitments for production. A few quick clarifying notes before I pull legal and CS in:

- When you say "phased monthly credit schedule," do you mean a temporary cap on monthly credit liability (a dollar cap) or lower % credits for breaches during the initial window?
- For batch/warmer windows, can you share expected daily time ranges (UTC) and average job durations so we can scope carveouts narrowly?

High-level we can propose a two-part approach:
1) A timeboxed ramp (90 days) where the payout schedule for availability breaches scales down linearly to the standard template. This keeps unit economics predictable for Aurora while giving you protection.
2) Explicit, auditable maintenance/batch windows (pre-declared) where certain latency SLO thresholds are relaxed; those windows will be subject to a short reporting requirement each month.

If that maps to what you need, I will draft a proposal (SLA_Amendment_Proposal_Aurora_v1.docx) with the exact % bands and a DocuSign-ready clause for legal review. Hope to have a draft to you by Thursday.

Rachel
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: SLA template amendment / uptime smoothing request

Marissa / Jordan — forwarding Aurora's ask. TL;DR: they want a 60–90 day ramp with reduced monthly credit exposure and defined latency carveouts for batch windows. Attached redlines.

Key questions for negotiation:
- Credit mechanics: dollar cap vs reduced % bands. My leaning: reduced % bands (keeps accounting simpler) but with an absolute monthly cap for the pilot (protects Redwood). Example proposal below.
- Timing: 90-day ramp to standard uptime (99.95%); pilot months counted from production cutover.
- Latency carveouts: allow pre-declared batch windows up to 2 hours/day where p99 is measured excluding those windows. Those windows must be scheduled and reported monthly.

Proposed phasing (draft):
- Month 0–1: availability baseline at 99.5% for remedy calculation; breach payouts capped at 25% of standard monthly credit liability.
- Month 2: availability baseline moves to 99.75%; breach payouts capped at 50% of standard liability.
- Month 3+: standard SLA baseline 99.95% and full credit liability.
- Operational review at day 30 and day 90 with the option to rebaseline if both sides agree in writing.

Attachments referenced: Aurora_SLA_Redlines.pdf (external), plus I'll attach our draft SLA amendment for signatures. Thoughts? If you approve, I'll send to legal and loop CS for the reporting hook.

-Rachel

--
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2026 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed SLA amendment (phased credits + latency fallback) — Aurora Analytics

Ethan / Priya —

Thanks for the redlines and for walking through the use case. We've drafted a targeted amendment that we think balances Aurora's ramp risk with Redwood's unit economics. Summary below; attached is the DocuSign-ready amendment (SLA_Amendment_Proposal_Aurora_v1.docx).

Summary (high level):
- Timeboxed ramp: 90 days from production cutover.
- Availability phasing and capped liability:
  * Month 0–1 (Day 0–30): availability baseline used for remedy calculation = 99.5%. Payouts for eligible availability breaches during this window are capped at 25% of the standard monthly credit liability.
  * Month 2 (Day 31–60): baseline = 99.75%; capped payouts = 50% of standard liability.
  * Month 3 (Day 61–90): baseline = 99.9%; capped payouts = 75% of standard liability.
  * Month 4+: standard baseline 99.95% and full credit liability.
- Latency fallback carveouts: Aurora may declare up to 2 pre-scheduled batch windows per 24-hr period (each up to 2 hours) where p99/p95 measurements exclude those windows for latency breach calculation. Windows must be declared in advance via the shared ops channel and included in monthly reports.
- Operational review: 30-day and 90-day formal reviews. Either party may request rebaseline if post-go-live metrics show sustained deviation; any change requires written agreement.
- Reporting: Redwood will provide a monthly availability and latency report with raw p95/p99 values and KV-cache warmup metrics for the declared windows.
- Legal: proposed amendment is intentionally narrow and timeboxed; it does not change Redwood's maintenance carveouts or security obligations.

Next steps:
1) If this captures Aurora's needs, sign the attached amendment via DocuSign link: https://rds.docuSign.net/signon?session=abc123-Aurora-DEAL-5941
2) Provide the initial set of batch window time ranges (UTC) so CS can configure reporting.
3) We will schedule the 30-day ops review for the first week after go-live.

Attachments: SLA_Amendment_Proposal_Aurora_v1.docx (Draft amendment, DocuSign-ready)

Happy to iterate; we aimed for predictable exposure for Aurora while preserving our SLA guardrails.

Best,
Rachel
